timestamp_origin: Browser relative to media start; host controller monotonic clock, separate origin
limitations: Fidelity admission and independent root review are separate prerequisites; extraction does not certify them.
Only the twelve new matched 2/4 Mbit/s positions are read or scored; historical and parent-cohort performance is neither substituted nor compared here.
Matched refers to the declared CPU-wrapper and namespace context, not matched fidelity; extraction does not establish bitrate as the sole cause of a difference.
Both candidates use lossy H.264 YUV420 Screen, all-IDR, 256 KiB tick, 30/30 timing, intra period 1 and BBR; fidelity equivalence is unproved.
Crop changes are not whole-screen FPS; Canvas readback is not scanout or whole-frame coherence.
Native process CPU, CDP endpoint-intersection CPU and UDP snapshots retain their distinct raw windows; short-lived browser CPU can be omitted.
RSS is the controller-reported final native sample, not independently reconstructed from raw RSS counters.
No overall winner, matched-quality, Guacamole, Internet or capacity claim is supported.
Private receipts prove recorded custody only; extraction does not repeat live process, device, namespace or socket audits.
Owner argv receipts do not record or prove parent-provided environment values; pinned helper/server/proxy arguments and report metadata retain independent CPU policy binding.
